content:
elaine: quick check  we want a single, teachable SDK pattern for streaming vs paging + retries. keep it thin across py/ts/go.

matt: yeah interested. one public shape that maps to native idioms per-lang?

elaine: exactly. propose two surface primitives: `stream()` (chunk-by-chunk) and `pages()` (page-at-a-time). both implemented on a small transport middleware stack (auth -> idempotency -> retry -> telemetry).

sanjay: middleware owning retries + idempotency seems right. do we attach idempotency tokens at request creation or transport layer?

taylor: transport layer. keep the language APIs clean. middleware will add `Idempotency-Key` for retryable calls and manage resume tokens for resumable streams.

matt: streaming+retries is tricky. if we retry a stream from start we might reemit items. how do we avoid duplicates or at least make it deterministic?

elaine: two streaming modes: transient and resumable. resumable streams include a tiny opaque resume token in chunk metadata. client can persist that and ask server to resume.

elaine: example sketches:

```python
# python
for chunk, resume in client.responses.stream(...):
    handle(chunk)
    if should_checkpoint:
        save(resume)
```

```ts
// ts
for await (const {item, resume} of client.responses.stream(...)) {
  // process and optionally save resume
}
```

sanjay: resume token shape: opaque, short (8-12 bytes base64), server TTL default 15m. client treats it as opaque string.

taylor: server validates token and enforces idempotency. client middleware sends saved token in a resume header when resuming.

matt: pagination: cursor objects vs page tokens. cursor objects are nice but cause cross-lang complexity.

elaine: prefer simple page tokens. `pages()` yields page objects with items + next_token. mapping to native iterators in each language.

elaine: sketches:

```python
for page in client.responses.pages(q, page_size=100):
    for item in page.items: ...
```

```ts
for await (const page of client.responses.pages({q, page_size:100})) {
  page.items.forEach(...)
}
```

```go
it := client.Responses().Pages(ctx, opts)
for it.Next() {
  page := it.Page()
  // iterate page.Items
}
```

sanjay: Go iterator + typed Page() is idiomatic. OK.

taylor: retries for pages: treat one page fetch as a single idempotent unit. retry middleware will retry the HTTP call; server must ensure page fetchs are idempotent.

elaine: streaming resumptions: middleware can resume by sending resume token + idempotency key. backoff semantics same as other retries.

matt: backward compatibility: older servers/clients might not support resume headers. fallback to query param `?resume=...` in addition to `X-Resume-Token` header so both sides can negotiate.

taylor: agreed. middleware should add both header and query param when resuming to maximize compatibility. server accepts either.

sanjay: telemetry: emit standardized events for retries, resume usage, page fetch latency, and attempt counts. shape: op, outcome, attempts, latency_ms. SDK exposes telemetry hook and logs by default.

elaine: yes, SDKs should call a telemetry callback and also emit structured events to Redwood Console integration if enabled. provide opt-out.

matt: long-term: unify conceptual middleware layers across languages (same order + semantics). build a minimal reference middleware in TS and port.

taylor: tests: fuzz resume tokens, simulate mid-stream truncation and resume, verify no silent duplicates beyond the resume boundary, ensure 429 -> respect Retry-After, respect client-side token-bucket rate budgets.

sanjay: on 429: middleware should read `Retry-After` and respect it. mirror existing token-bucket behavior in JS to py/go.

eleine: (typo fix) elaine: decision checklist for RFC follow-up:
- final API sketches for `stream()` and `pages()` per-lang  OK
- resume token format & TTL (opaque base64, 15m)  OK
- transport middleware: retry + idempotency + resume injection  OK
- telemetry events & SDK hooks  OK
- backward-compat via header + query param  OK
- test matrix (fuzz, 429/500/stream truncation)  OK

matt: all thumbs up. add migration guidance: when to choose pages vs stream (memory tradeoffs, checkpoint cost, server state).

taylor: I'll draft the follow-up doc with compatibility table + test plan and assign ports for py/go. will ping when ready @here.

elaine: thanks all. adding action: add to SDK surface RFC and create tracking tickets. :raised_hands:

ci-bot: Reminder: created ticket RFC-9292 to track SDK middleware and resume work

matt: sweet, closing this thread. :thumbsup:
